stops.segment: From the Meuse to the Paraná
stops.stop: Paris, the school that cannot be named
stops.date_confidence: Genuine and unresolved contradiction, carried open. stops.segment: The Province Builds Itself a Capital
stops.stop: Buenos Aires, ten founders or nine
stops.date_confidence: The founding date, 18 March 1886, is firm on both sides. Dormal's presence is not. The legislative report says 'Fue uno de los diez miembros fundadores... junto a Ernesto Bunge y Juan Antonio Buschiazzo'; hilariobooks.com repeats that he was a founder. But juan_antonio_buschiazzo.journey.json names nine founders from an independent roster and Dormal is not among them, and the legislative report's own enumeration likewise runs to nine names without his. The contradiction is real and is left unresolved. The founding venue is unknown; the coordinate is the general city pin.

stops.date_confidence: Attested by argentina.gob.ar's monument page for the Cine-Teatro Ópera, which dates the original theatre to 1872, names Émile Landois as its architect, and confirms Dormal's 1888 modification giving it a 'suntuosa imagen Beaux-Arts', with demolition in 1935 and Alberto Bourdon's replacement reopened 7 August 1936. stops.segment: Inheriting the Dead Men's Drawings
stops.stop: Teatro Colón, the third architect
stops.date_confidence: Attested. es.wikipedia's Historia del Teatro Colón puts Dormal's assumption of the direction in February 1905 following Meano's death; no day is given. Meano was shot on 1 June 1904 at the age of forty-four, per the theatre's institutional history. Tamburini won the bid in 1889 and laid the stone on 25 May 1890, and francesco_tamburini.journey.json corrects the common Argentine claim that he died the same year: en.wikipedia and it.wikipedia both put his death in 1891. His birth year is itself contested, 1846 against 1848, so the 'aged 44' figure that seeds the architects'-curse legend is not securely establishable. stops.stop: Teatro Colón, opened with Aida
stops.date_confidence: Attested. es.wikipedia's Historia del Teatro Colón and teatrocolon.org.ar both give 25 May 1908 and Verdi's Aida, and the theatre's own history records that sections including the Salón Dorado remained unfinished at the opening. The date is eighteen years to the day from Tamburini's cornerstone of 25 May 1890, both dates being the national holiday. stops.segment: Inheriting the Dead Men's Drawings
stops.stop: Teatro Colón, sat for Jules Lagae
stops.date_confidence: Attested by weboeba.com's Dormal entry, which gives the whole chain: a bronze bust forty centimetres high modelled by Jules Lagae in 1909, donated to the Teatro Colón by the sculptor's son, formalised by 'Decreto - Ordenanza n.o 9966 del 12 de agosto de 1962', inaugurated in September 1962 in the foyer entered from Calle Libertad. An AGORHA/INHA record that might document the modelling returned 403 and es.wikipedia is silent on the bust; neither silence is evidence against it. Where Lagae modelled him, and whether from life, is not stated. The stop sits at the building the bronze ends up in.

stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Buenos Aires city heritage page for Florida 466, which names Julio Dormal as architect and says the building 'fue inaugurado en 1913'. No month is given. Coordinate corrected: Nominatim resolves Florida 466, San Nicolás, to -34.60265, -58.37531, and a working value of -34.5996, -58.3746 landed near Plaza San Martín, about 340 m off. The neighbouring Peña-Blaye residence, later the Sociedad Rural Argentina, is attributed to him by the Wikimedia Commons category but by no heritage record fetched here, and its street number and date are unconfirmed.

stops.segment: The Coast, the Council, and the Rented City
stops.stop: Florida 468, the Richmond opens downstairs
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by es.wikipedia's Confitería Richmond, which gives 17 November 1917 and the address Florida 468, 'en la planta baja de un edificio diseñado por el arquitecto belga Jules Dormal junto a la Residencia Peña'; the city heritage page confirms 1917 and the Grupo de Florida association. Note the two-number discrepancy: the building is catalogued at 466, the confitería at 468. Coordinate as corrected for Florida 466 above. Dormal's own presence in the café is not documented.
notes: hard triggers (disputed) discounted: the day is explicitly attested and their clause names no date, year, month or number (it concerns the pin, the house or the sources)

stops.segment: The Coast, the Council, and the Rented City
stops.stop: Arroyo 1130, called in over another man's staircase
stops.date_confidence: Attested by argentina.gob.ar's Palacio Pereda page, which has Louis Martin creating the initial Beaux-Arts design and 'Julio Dormal made revisions at the request of owner Celedonio Pereda'; es.wikipedia's Palacio Pereda dates the replacement to 1919, with the interior and staircase design as the cause, and work running 1920-1936. The legislative report's 'Celestino Pereda' is the source's own error. Its 'Desde 1944' for the Brazilian residence is also corrected: the property passed to Brazil after Pereda's death in 1945. Coordinate corrected to Arroyo 1130, -34.591755, -58.383447; a working value put it at Cerrito 1350, nearly a kilometre west.

stops.segment: The House on Plaza San Martín
stops.stop: San Martín 1137, the front he puts on himself
stops.date_confidence: Date unresolved and both years are carried: infobae (3 November 2024) gives 1920, other sources give 1913, and the arquitectos-franceses blog that describes the building in most detail gives no construction year at all. The architectural description is confirmed verbatim by that blog: 'cuatro largas columnas corintias de fuste liso', 'cuatro bajorrelieves con motivos diferentes donde los protagonistas son querubines', 'Dos pares de columnas... de orden jónico', 'un frontis triangular'. The structural figures come from a 2024 sale listing and are advertised rather than surveyed. Coordinate corrected to Nominatim's San Martín 1137, -34.59449, -58.37432; the geography and afterlife working values disagreed with each other by about 200 m and neither was right.

stops.segment: The House on Plaza San Martín
stops.stop: San Martín 1137, the will written by hand
stops.date_confidence: The 1922 handwritten will is attested by his descendant Magdalena Paz Miguens at the 2024 centenary, reported by fmradiocultura.com.ar, which says he wrote it in perfect Spanish entirely in his own hand and signed it Julio Dormal. The text has never been published and was not seen. No day or month is given. The family counts are also from that report: three marriages, ten children, six grandchildren, thirty great-grandchildren, over 250 great-great-grandchildren. The legislative report gives two marriages, Amalia Peña then Elina Sosa Díaz, and three children, Carmen, Julia and Carlos. The two counts are irreconcilable as they stand and both are carried. The place of writing is assumed to be his house.

Born in 1846 with no day recorded, he is seventy-seven or seventy-eight. Coordinate as corrected for San Martín 1137.

stops.segment: The House on Plaza San Martín
stops.stop: Cementerio de la Recoleta, the vault that is no longer there
stops.date_confidence: Burial at Recoleta is attested by the legislative report, which says he was buried 'en su bóveda en la Recoleta', and by recoletacemetery.com, which specifies the mausoleum of his second wife, Elena or Elina Sosa Díaz. The exhumation chain is tagged reconstruction by that source itself: cemetery records showing cremation in 1989 and remains 'likely placed inside the Dolmas Arévalo vault, though the reason remains undocumented', with neither tomb standing today. No official cemetery response was obtained. The burial day is not recorded and 24 March orders it. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Recoleta pin in juan_antonio_buschiazzo.journey.json; pedro_benoit.journey.json carries -34.5878, -58.3932 for the same cemetery and the divergence is noted, not resolved.
